related_questions.question: How do I check my child's credit?

text_blocks.snippet: To check if a child has a credit report, parents or guardians can contact the three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion) to request a search of their databases. Children under 18 generally don't have credit reports, but one might exist if an identity thief uses their information, or if the child is an authorized user on an adult's account.
snippet_highlighted_words: contact the three major credit bureaus (Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion) to request a search of their databases

text_blocks.snippet: This video explains how to check your child's credit report and potential signs of identity theft:

list.title: 1. Gather necessary documents:
list.snippet: This typically includes the child's birth certificate, Social Security card, and proof of your relationship (like a utility bill with your shared address). You may also need a copy of your government-issued ID.

list.title: 2. Contact the credit bureaus:
list.snippet: Each bureau has a process for handling minor requests. You can usually find the necessary forms on their websites or contact them directly by phone.

list.title: 3. Submit your request:
list.snippet: Provide the required documentation and information to the credit bureaus.

list.title: 4. Review the results:
list.snippet: If a credit report exists, the bureau will contact you for further information or to provide the report.

text_blocks.snippet: This video explains how to check your child's credit report and what information you need to provide to the credit bureaus:

list.title: AnnualCreditReport.com:
list.snippet: This is the only authorized website for free credit reports for adults. Children under 13 will not be able to use this site.

list.title: Identity Theft:
list.snippet: Be vigilant about potential identity theft. If you suspect your child's identity has been compromised, take steps to freeze their credit report and monitor their credit activity.

list.title: Authorized Users:
list.snippet: Children can be added as authorized users on credit card accounts, which can create a credit report for them. This is usually done with the parent's consent.

list.title: Security Freeze:
list.snippet: If you are concerned about unauthorized use of your child's identity, you can request a security freeze on their credit report. This prevents new credit accounts from being opened in their name.
